message.content: **Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and decided to buy, then placed one order: **buy 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $223.00**, which filled at $223.00 for a total of $9,812 — within the $10,000 per-order cap, and well under the $20,000 daily total. My reasoning rested on the reported fundamentals: FY2024 revenue of **$391,035 million** (+2% year over year, driven by Services up 13% to $96,169 million), **operating income of $123,216 million** (operating margin ~31.5%), **gross margin expansion to 46.2%** from 44.1%, **operating cash flow of $118,254 million**, and **diluted EPS of $6.08**; net income of **$93,736 million** was down about 3% year over year, but that decline is attributable almost entirely to a **one-time $10.2 billion net income tax charge** related to the European Commission State Aid Decision, not to operating deterioration — operating income actually rose. The balance sheet remains very strong ($140.8 billion of unrestricted cash and marketable securities), and the company repurchased $95.0 billion of stock in fiscal 2024 (499 million shares), shrinking the share count and supporting per-share value. The limit price of $223.00 was set just above the current quote (last $222.70, ask $222.72) to stay close to market while ensuring execution. One important caveat worth flagging: the filing contains an internal inconsistency — the "Highlights" line and the total net sales row of the Consolidated Statements of Operations state $94,930 million, which contradicts the segment and product tables and the arithmetic of the statements themselves (products $294,866M + services $96,169M − cost of sales $210,352M = gross margin $180,683M, implying $391,035M of revenue); I treated $391,035 million as the correct figure, consistent with the SEC filing lookup. The account still holds 100 shares of MSFT, no money was moved out, and only AAPL was traded, in line with the mandate.
